aboutAppContent: The application for assessing the critical condition of patients in the emergency department of Thammasat Chaloem Phra Kiat Hospital is a newly developed software designed as a tool for evaluating the critical condition of patients using the MEWS score calculation method, which will replace the manual tool used for recording patient crisis condition assessments.
failedToAddPatient: Failed to add the patient to monitored state
failedToRemovePatient: Failed to removed patient from monitored state
name: Name
newPassword: New Password (Leave blank to keep existing)
nurseIDMustBeANumber: Nurse ID must be a number!
nursingHigh: • Observe and assess the patient's condition, record V/S every 15-30 minutes, and monitor according to nursing standards. Report to the shift supervisor and provide nursing care as appropriate. • Report to Intern doctor or 1st call to assess the patient's condition within 30 minutes and provide medical instructions. • Assess the patient and record V/S every 30 minutes for 3 consecutive times. If the MEWS score remains 5 for 3 consecutive times, record V/S every 15 minutes. • If the condition does not improve, report to 2nd call/3rd call doctor to assess the patient within 15 minutes and provide medical instructions. • Consider increasing recording of I/O every 2 hours. If urine output is < 50 cc in 2 hours, report to the doctor. • If the MEWS score remains 5 for 3 consecutive times, consult the doctor to consider transferring the patient to the critical care unit.
nursingLow: • Observe and assess the patient's condition, record V/S every 8 hours, and monitor according to nursing standards.
nursingLowMedium: • Observe and assess the patient's condition, record V/S every 4 hours, and monitor according to nursing standards. Report to the shift supervisor. • Report to Intern doctor or 1st call to assess the patient's condition within 30 minutes and provide medical instructions.
nursingMedium: • Observe and assess the patient's condition, record V/S every 2 hours, and monitor according to nursing standards. Report to the shift supervisor and provide nursing care as appropriate. • Report to Intern doctor or 1st call to assess the patient's condition within 30 minutes and provide medical instructions. • Assess the patient and record V/S every 2 hours for 3 consecutive times. If the MEWS score remains 3 for 3 consecutive times, record V/S every 1 hour. • If the condition does not improve, report to 2nd call/3rd call doctor to assess the patient within 30 minutes and provide medical instructions.
nursingMediumHigh: • Observe and assess the patient's condition, record V/S every 30 minutes to 1 hour, and monitor according to nursing standards. Report to the shift supervisor and provide nursing care as appropriate. • Report to Intern doctor or 1st call to assess the patient's condition within 30 minutes and provide medical instructions. • Assess the patient and record V/S every 1 hour for 3 consecutive times. If the MEWS score remains 4 for 3 consecutive times, record V/S every 15-30 minutes. • If the condition does not improve, report to 2nd call/3rd call doctor to assess the patient within 15 minutes and provide medical instructions. • Consider increasing recording of I/O every 4 hours. If urine output is < 100 cc in 4 hours, report to the doctor.

outOfRange.heartRate: Heart rate is out of range (30-200 bpm).
